verdict.rationale: Railway documents its own isolated deployment targets: unlimited environments, per-pull-request previews, and an MCP server that lets AI assistants manage environments. That gives an AI-native user a non-production place to test. This is environment-level sandbox isolation rather than a dry-run mode, but the evidence never states that these environments keep production data separate. missing for 10: explicit documentation that preview/non-production environments isolate databases and data from production, details on seeding or cloning test data, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Unlimited environments mean everyone can ship simultaneously.
Every pull request gets its own preview. No surprises after merge.
It lets AI assistants create projects, deploy templates, manage environments, pull variables, and redeploy services.
